newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN AMRO HOARE GOVETT RATES RICHTER A 'BUY'.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO HOARE GOVETT RATES RICHTER A 'BUY'.

text.p: ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett said on Tuesday that 1996 results of Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Rt were in line with ABN-AMRO's expectations and thus maintained a 'buy' recommendation.
"Overall, results were very much in line with our expectations," Tommy Erdei, ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett's Budapest-based analyst said in a company update.

Richter published its preliminary IAS 1996 earnings report on February 11 and reported its sales rising to 36.74 billion forints from 27.39 billion in 1995, while its net profit grew to 11.35 billion forints from 7.88 billion in 1995.
The company's operating margin rose to 20 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from 16.9 percent in the last quarter of 1995, but fell from 21.3 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
Richter'gross margins for the fourth quarter declined to 57 percent from 61.4 percent in the third quarter.
"We see two principal factors behind the lower margins: the sudden strength of the U.S. dollar and the company's inability to pass on cost increases in full to the export markets," Erdei said.
The U.S. unit has a 70 percent weighting in the National Bank of Hungary's currency basket against which the forint floats while exports account for around two-thirds of Richter's total sales.

The analyst said ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett adjusted its 1997 forecasts for Richter downwards, reducing net income by 5.8 percent to 14.61 billion forints in the light of stronger-than-expected erosion of margins in the fourth quarter of 1996.
In the first quarter of 1997, Erdei expects gross margins to improve.

"In 1997 Q1 we see margins improving considerably (to 62.9 percent) as a result of the government-authorised January 1, 1997 10 percent average price increase for pharmaceuticals producers from January 1," the analyst said.
"Going forward, we expect to see margins steady as the dollar halts its steep increase and also as the company continues to increase exports to markets where price regulation is much more moderate."
Erdei said he expected the Q1 1997 operating margins to jump to 27.5 percent.
